title: Power Rankings: After the break, Pistons still No. 1
heading: 2007-08 Power Rankings: Week 16
author: Marc Stein

rankings.summaryHtml: One e-mailer, responding to last week's comment, claims Detroit's craving to be dissed was "so last year." Which tempted us yet again to test that theory by dropping the Pistons and their 10-game win streak to No. 2.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Celts just went 7-2 without Garnett, sport a 16-0 record against the West and are about to welcome KG back to the only team going that still has a single-digit loss total. Can the committee (of one) call itself crazy?

rankings.summaryHtml: Getting Kidd isn't about making an "over-the-top" move in the West because there are no over-the-top moves in the West. This is a move Dallas had to make to keep from slipping further away from the top.

rankings.summaryHtml: The Rockets' big moves, obviously, were bringing in Adelman and deciding not to trade T-Mac. But those will be regarded as pretty shrewd moves, too, if Houston can keep this up, at a tidy 17-4 in 2008.

rankings.summaryHtml: Now that the playoff dream is really starting to slip away, it seems like a good time to remind folks that Portland's Cinderellas are just the second team in history to win at least 10 games in a row after a 50-loss season.
